title: Finite geometric cohomology model and normalized scalar comparison
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, a separable closure $k^s$, and $G=\operatorname{Aut}_k(k^s)$. Let $X/k$ be separated of finite type. Let $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be an algebraic closure with its norm topology and $E\subset\Omega$ finite over $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Put $C(P)=\{f\in C(P,\Omega):f(P)\text{ lies in one finite subextension}\}$ and $B(P)=C(P,\Omega)$, and let $c:C\to B$ be inclusion [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed, def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. Put $A=\underline E$ and, for a condensed ring $R$, $R_X=p_X^*R$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use internal ordinary derived relative tensor [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. For a bounded constructible $V\in D(A_X)$ in the finite constant local model convention [sk-def-sfb-constructible], put $K_A=\mathcal K_A(V)$ and $K_R=\mathcal K_R(R_X\otimes^L_{A_X}V)$ for $R=C,B$, with the equivariant geometric derived section functors of [lem-sfb-condensed-galois-global-descent].

The object $K_A$ is bounded in $D(\mathcal A_G(A))$. For every integer $q$ there is a finite-dimensional norm-topological $E$-vector space $W_q$ with continuous $E$-linear $G$-action such that $H^q(K_A)$ is its condensed module $P\mapsto C(P,W_q)$, equivariantly; $W_q=0$ outside a finite interval.

For $R=C,B$, the actual derived coefficient projection morphism
$$\beta_R:R\otimes_A^L K_A\longrightarrow K_R$$
is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal A_G(R))$. This morphism is specified, not an unspecified isomorphism: it is the transpose, under the derived adjunction $R\otimes_A^L-\dashv\operatorname{Res}_{A\to R}$ on equivariant derived categories, of the composite $K_A=\mathcal K_A(V)\xrightarrow{\mathcal K_A(\eta_V)}\mathcal K_A(\operatorname{Res}(R_X\otimes^L_{A_X}V))\to\operatorname{Res}\mathcal K_R(R_X\otimes^L_{A_X}V)$, where $\eta_V$ is the derived scalar-extension unit, represented on a K-flat resolution by $v\mapsto1\otimes v$, and the second arrow is the canonical comparison of the derived geometric section functors with the exact scalar restriction. Let $\kappa:\mathcal K_C(C_X\otimes^L_{A_X}V)\to\operatorname{Res}_c\mathcal K_B(B_X\otimes^L_{A_X}V)$ be $\mathcal K_C$ of the morphism $C_X\otimes^L_{A_X}V\to\operatorname{Res}_{c_X}(B_X\otimes^L_{A_X}V)$ induced by $z\otimes v\mapsto c_X(z)\otimes v$, followed by the same canonical comparison with scalar restriction. Then the square $\operatorname{Res}_c(\beta_B)\circ\gamma=\kappa\circ\beta_C$ commutes in $D(\mathcal A_G(C))$, where $\gamma:C\otimes_A^LK_A\to\operatorname{Res}_c(B\otimes_A^LK_A)$ is induced by $z\otimes v\mapsto c(z)\otimes v$; in particular it commutes after further restriction to $A$. The assertions are natural in $V$ and compatible with shifts. They do not assert that $C_X\to B_X$ is an isomorphism or flat, or that $\Omega$ is complete.

proof.text: Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and write $a:X\to s$ for the structure map. By [lem-sfb-field-action-derived-section-transport] use the exact normalized equivalences $E_R$ from field module sheaves to condensed $G$-modules. They identify $\mathcal K_R$ with $D(E_R)Ra_{*,R}$, preserve scalar adjunction units and counits, and identify the specified $\beta_R$ with the canonical coefficient projection for $a$. Thus this is a comparison of the actual maps of the statement. The same input identifies forgetting $G$ with geometric derived sections over $X^s$ and makes it an exact conservative functor; below this permits detecting an isomorphism after forgetting the action.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dc-lower-star-preserves] with coefficient $\underline E$ to $a:X\to s$. Its hypotheses are met: $\underline E$ for the finite normed $E$ is one of its coefficient rings, and $X$, $s$ and $a$ lie in the setting of the item ($k$ of characteristic $p\ne\ell$, separated finite-type $k$-schemes). Its input is bounded constructible in the stratified local-finite-presentation sense, whereas $V$ is given in the finite constant local model sense; a finite constant local model is locally finitely presented by [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model], on the same constructible strata, so $V$ qualifies. Hence every $H^q(Ra_{*,A}V)$ is constructible in the local-finite-presentation sense, and only finitely many are nonzero. Since $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian and $\underline E$ carries certificate (i), [lem-sfb-adic-constructibility-predicate-comparison] converts this into the finite constant local model sense of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. On the one-point scheme $s$ the only nonempty stratum is $s$ itself, and a finitely presented $E$-module is a finite-dimensional vector space, hence free of finite rank. So on a pro-étale cover each $H^q(Ra_{*,A}V)$ is $A_{U_i}^{n_i}$, that is, lisse [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. The last clause of [lem-sfb-field-action-derived-section-transport] gives a finite-dimensional norm-topological $E$-representation $W_q$ of $G$ realizing it. T-exactness of $D(E_A)$ identifies this realization with $H^q(K_A)$. Since there are only finitely many nonzero cohomology sheaves, choose $W_q=0$ outside the same finite interval. This proves boundedness in the equivariant category, without taking arithmetic invariants.

proof.text: For $R=C$, apply [lem-sfb-qlbar-direct-image-comparison] to $a$ and the bounded (hence bounded-below) complex $V$. The morphism is qcqs because it is separated of finite type; in particular the source is qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine]. This theorem uses exactly the finite-subextension-valued ring $C$, not $B$. It says the counit-adjoint projection is an isomorphism in the target module derived category. Applying $D(E_C)$ and the unit/counit normalization in [lem-sfb-field-action-derived-section-transport] proves that the actual $\beta_C$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Paragraph (3), geometric finite-coefficient cohomology and coefficient projection; agent expansion, with the remaining norm generator input explicitly isolated.

proof.text: For $R=B$, forget $G$ using [lem-sfb-field-action-derived-section-transport]. The resulting map is the coefficient projection $B\otimes_A^L Rp_{X^s*}V^s\to Rp_{X^s*}(B_{X^s}\otimes^L_{A_{X^s}}V^s)$, where $V^s=u^*V$. Pullback is exact by [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-main], so $H^q(V^s)=u^*H^q(V)$ and $V^s$ is bounded. By [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model] each $H^q(V)$ is constructible in the local-finite-presentation sense, and [lem-weil-pbc-module-constructible-pullback] shows that $u^*H^q(V)$ is again constructible in that sense. The scheme $X^s$ is separated of finite type over the separably closed positive-characteristic field $k^s$, hence Noetherian, so [lem-sfb-adic-constructibility-predicate-comparison] (certificate (i) for $\underline E$) puts $V^s$ in $\Dbc(X^s,E)$ of [sk-def-sfb-constructible], the finite constant local model convention used by the generator lemma. By [det-lem-integral-models-generators](1), $V^s$ is obtained by finitely many cones and shifts from objects $Q=(a_!L_0)[1/\ell]$, with $a:S\hookrightarrow X^s$ locally closed and $L_0$ lisse finite free over $\mathcal O_{E,S}$. The coefficient field remains this same $E$; no field descent of the whole complex is being asserted.

proof.text: For each generator $Q$ just obtained, [lem-sfb-supported-lattice-norm-projection], applied with $K=k^s$ and $T=X^s$, proves invertibility of exactly this projection map. To pass through the finite construction, fix the coefficient object $B$ and use [lem-sfb-ringed-projection-first-shift]: projection is a natural transformation of exact functors in the geometric input, compatible with its shifts and the third arrows of triangles. Thus the isomorphism locus contains every shift of a generator and is closed under cones by [lem-sf-triangle-two-out-of-three]. Induction on the finite number of shifts and cones in step 4 proves invertibility for $V^s$. Exact conservativity of forgetting $G$ from step 1 now proves invertibility of $\beta_B$ in $D(\mathcal A_G(B))$. This uses no commutation of tensor with an infinite totalization.

proof.text:
It remains to check the prescribed square rather than choose unrelated isomorphisms. Work first on $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and use the canonical coefficient maps $A_s\to C_s\xrightarrow{c_s}B_s$. The normalized projections are the $\chi$ of [lem-pur-ringed-coefficient-projection-cocycle]. Its cocycle identity identifies the projection for the composite $A_s\to B_s$ with the successive projections for $A_s\to C_s$ and $C_s\to B_s$, under balanced tensor associativity. Precompose the latter identity with the scalar unit $C_s\otimes^L_{A_s}Ra_*V\to\operatorname{Res}_{c_s}(B_s\otimes^L_{A_s}Ra_*V)$. The scalar adjunction triangle identity then gives
$$\operatorname{Res}_{c_s}(\chi_{A,B})\circ\gamma_s=\kappa_s\circ\chi_{A,C}.$$
More explicitly, the transpose of either side is $Ra_*V\to\operatorname{Res}_{A,B}Ra_{*,B}(B_X\otimes^L_{A_X}V)$ induced by the same unit $v\mapsto1\otimes v$; the route through $C$ sends it to $1\otimes v\mapsto c(1)\otimes v=1\otimes v$. Uniqueness of adjoints proves equality of these derived arrows. Transport by the coefficient-compatible equivalences of [lem-sfb-field-action-derived-section-transport] gives exactly $\operatorname{Res}_c(\beta_B)\circ\gamma=\kappa\circ\beta_C$. This is an equality in the $C$-equivariant derived category and therefore remains one after restriction to $A$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), geometric finite-coefficient cohomology and coefficient projection; agent expansion, with the remaining norm generator input explicitly isolated.

proof.text: All projections in the preceding steps are the counit-adjoint maps. Naturality in $V$ follows from naturality of the derived scalar unit and the comparison with restriction, preserved by the normalized transport. Compatibility with the canonical shifts follows from [lem-sfb-ringed-projection-first-shift] and the shift compatibility in [lem-pur-ringed-coefficient-projection-cocycle] and [lem-sfb-field-action-derived-section-transport]. These give the claimed naturality and shift assertion for both isomorphisms and their square. If $V=0$ or $X=\varnothing$, every geometric object and map here is zero; if $G=1$, transport forgets no action and the same proof applies.
